images.alt:
Infographic about navigable rivers. 
What is a navigable river?
•	Sufficient width and depth for 
	boats, barges, punts, or rafts.
•	It need not be navigable at all 
	times.
Who owns the riverbed?
•	The crown normally owns the 
	riverbed.
•	Iwi and hapū with mana whenua 
	may be granted customary 
	marine title rights near a river 
	mouth.
Public access rights
•	You can usually enter navigable 
	rivers legally.
•	Generally, access will only be 
	opposed if there’s a conflicting 
	use, such as hydroelectric 
	damming or another right.

post.text: It’s worth noting that the recent Supreme Court case about navigable rivers does not change public access rights to those rivers. Everyone can continue to have free public access on the marine and coastal area, including the mouth of navigable rivers.  www.herengaanuku.govt.nz/types-of-acc...
